get_local_news.description: Get the latest headlines about one place: a town, city, region or country. Google works out which place you mean, so the result says which one it settled on: ask for 'Bay Area' and it reads 'San Francisco Bay Area'. A name it cannot place comes back as an error rather than as the country's news, which is what the feed does on its own.
get_local_news.name: get_local_news

parameters.description: The town, city, region or country to read the news of. Add the state or country when the name is a common one; there are dozens of Springfields.
parameters.name: place

parameters.description: Which Google News edition to read. An edition is a country and a language together: it sets what the headlines are written in and which country's news they are chosen for. Defaults to the United States in English.
parameters.name: edition

parameters.description: How many articles to return, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 10. Google decides how many a feed holds (around 40 for the front page, 70 for a section or a place, and about a hundred for a search) and every result says how many it found, so you can tell a short list from a low limit.
parameters.name: limit

get_section_headlines.description: Get the latest headlines from one section of Google News: World, National, Business, Technology, Entertainment, Sports, Science or Health. National means whichever country the edition is for, so the same step reads US news on the United States edition and French news on the French one.

search_news.description: Search Google News for articles matching some words, optionally narrowed to a date range or to particular news sites. This searches the whole index rather than the ranked front page, and returns about a hundred articles: the step behind a daily brief on a subject, or a watch on a company name.

parameters.description: The words to search for. Put a phrase in quotes to match it exactly ("supply chain"), and put a minus in front of a word to leave it out (-opinion).
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only articles published on or after this day. Leave empty for no earliest date. Google matches by day rather than to the minute.
parameters.name: published_after

parameters.description: Only articles published on or before this day. Leave empty for no latest date.

parameters.description: Only articles from these news sites, separated by commas. A full link to one of a site's articles is fine; it is reduced to the site for you. Leave empty to search every publisher Google indexes.

description: Read Google News: the front page, any of the eight sections, the news for a town or city, or a search across everything Google indexes, in any of its 80 country-and-language editions. Every article comes back as a headline, the publisher, when it was published and a link, so a workflow can summarise a morning brief, watch a company name, or post a topic to a channel. No account or API key is required.
